text: The device hums. A stone hall on a hill, and worried faces everywhere. This is Gibeah, the home of King Saul.
Now the Spirit of the LORD departed from Saul, and a spirit of distress from the LORD began to torment him.

speaker: Servant
text: Let our lord command your servants here to seek out someone who can skillfully play the harp.

speaker: King Saul
text: Find me someone who plays well, and bring him to me.

speaker: Servant
text: I have seen a son of Jesse of Bethlehem who knows how to play the harp. … and the LORD is with him.
Notice what the servant said about David. He played well, but the most important thing was this: the LORD was with him.

speaker: Messenger
text: Send me your son David, who is with the sheep.

speaker: Jesse
text: The king has sent for my son! {name}, help me load the donkey: bread, a skin of wine, and a young goat.
And Jesse took a donkey loaded with bread, a skin of wine, and one young goat and sent them to Saul with his son David.
When David came to Saul and entered his service, Saul loved him very much, and David became his armor-bearer.
And whenever the spirit from God came upon Saul, David would pick up his harp and play. Then Saul would find relief and feel better, and the spirit of distress would depart from him.
David had already been anointed as the next king. Yet here he serves the king he will one day replace, using his gift to help someone who is hurting.
